body.statement: If \(G\) is acyclic, every active graph reached by transitions (1)--(4) of \(\mathsf{SC\mbox{-}CTFID}\) is acyclic.  Consequently cyclic-terminal transitions (6)--(7), \(\mathsf{SATerm}\), and the obstruction \(O\) are unreachable.  Every remaining terminal subproblem is passed by transition (5), with the inherited fixed order, to CTFID, and the returned expressions or acyclic certificates are composed only by transitions (1)--(4).  Literal equality with the output of a separately implemented CTFID is not asserted without a common formal transition system and expression normal form.
body.justification: The standard acyclic special case prevents a competing semantics on familiar inputs.
body.gap: CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 settles the acyclic case; the strict reduction claim is that every added source-aware cyclic transition is vacuous and the outputs coincide exactly.
body.consumer: Existing cfid users retain backward-compatible outputs when no directed feedback is present.
body.proof_tex: Transitions (1)--(4) delete event rows, restrict to ancestors, split a partition, or extract an available regime factor.  On the directed graph they only delete vertices or edges and take induced subgraphs.  A directed cycle in any resulting graph would therefore already be a directed cycle in \(G\), contradicting acyclicity.  Thus every pending active graph is acyclic.  The guard for transition (6), which requires an original-cycle-labeled terminal, is never satisfied; transition (7) can only glue an output of (6), so it is also unreachable.  Since \(O\) is emitted only by \(\mathsf{SATerm}\), \(O\) is unreachable as well.  The first applicable terminal rule is consequently (5), which by \(\text{def:algorithm-handle}\) invokes CTFID with the inherited order.  All later operations are the sums, products, cancellations, and ordered compositions already performed by transitions (1)--(4).  This proves the stated operational reduction.  The frozen core contains no formal transition system or canonical expression normal form for a separate CTFID implementation, so literal output equality cannot be deduced and is not claimed.
